thread.title: West suburban woman recovers nearly $4K after fake airline support scam
thread.title_full: West suburban woman recovers nearly $4K after fake airline support scam

author: ABC7Chicago
title: West suburban woman recovers nearly $4K after fake airline support scam
text:
A River Forest woman says she lost thousands of dollars after attempting to change an airline reservation and allegedly being directed to a fraudulent phone number.
Thursday, July 23, 2026 3:53AMRIVER FOREST, Ill. -- A River Forest woman says she lost thousands of dollars after attempting to change an airline reservation and allegedly being directed to a fraudulent phone number, highlighting concerns about travel scams involving fake airline and hotel call centers.
Scammers posing as travel representatives may offer what appear to be better deals or assistance, but instead seek to obtain consumers' payment information. Joanna Moroz Domino said she was trying to change an Icelandair flight from Chicago to the United Kingdom. Because the ticket was nonrefundable, she was unable to make the change through normal channels. Moroz Domino said she received an email regarding the airline's decision and followed a link to a live chat.
"So the guy on live chat says this person will be able to help you; you are a frequent flier. Sorry about this experience," Moroz Domino said. She said she believes someone in what she described as a legitimate Icelandair chat provided the fraudulent phone number. Icelandair, however, said it has not found evidence that the number "...originated from Icelandair systems or official communication channels.
" Moroz Domino described the person she spoke with as "very helpful, very apologetic, saying he'll be able to help me. " She said the individual claimed he could "override" the nonrefundable tickets by logging into her account, upgrading her to a more expensive "flexible" ticket and then canceling the reservation. Moroz Domino said the arrangement was actually a scam that resulted in her paying approximately $4,000 more for the purported flexible tickets.
Moroz Domino said she was never refunded the approximately $2,000 she had already paid Icelandair for the nonrefundable tickets; although she did receive a refund for taxes. A voicemail from the fake airline support stated, "This is Ethan calling from Icelandair support desk ... that is just part of the taxes I was calling explain to you.
" Icelandair said that all "...subsequent communications regarding a purported refund were conducted directly with this third party... " and not with the airline. The company added that it takes incidents involving brand impersonation and fraud seriously and "...encourages customers to verify that they are communicating through contact information published on Icelandair's official website.
" After ABC7 Chicago's I-Team contacted American Express, Moroz Domino said the credit card company decided to refund nearly $4,000 she paid in the fraudulent transaction. Moroz Domino said American Express initially told her she had waited beyond the 60-day reporting window.
However, she said the alleged scammer had delayed the process by telling her that ticket refunds would take time. In a statement, American Express said: "We take these matters seriously and review all fraud and dispute claims carefully. We encourage customers to verify payment instructions through a trusted source before sending funds or sharing account information.
"The person who answered identified the operation as an airline reservation desk, but didn't answer questions. Cybersecurity experts warn that fake travel call center numbers posing as airlines and hotels can appear in online search results. Moroz Domino said she hopes others can learn from her experience.
"I think is horrendous. And I want other people to know that you can't trust whoever you're talking to," she said. Experts also warn that fake travel representatives may send phishing messages claiming there is a problem with travel plans in an attempt to obtain personal or payment information.
Consumers are encouraged to contact airlines and hotels directly and obtain phone numbers through official apps or by calling the number listed on the back of an airline or hotel credit card.
